title: Consolidated focus zones, ARIA-live notifications, and contrast ramp audit for virtualized lists and composite controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Recent accessibility spot checks uncovered inconsistent keyboard behavior across composite controls (action menus, inline editors, toggle groups) and weak ARIA announcement behavior in virtualized table/list experiences. This ticket consolidates a set of design-system-level fixes: formalize focus-zone patterns for composite components, introduce a documented ARIA-live pattern for virtualized row updates and inline validation, and recalibrate the color-contrast token ramp to meet WCAG 2.1 AA and address edge cases for compact density charts and table row states. Outcome: a small set of design tokens, component spec updates, a VPAT evidence bundle, and a follow-up engineering backlog for runtime integration and CI checks.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens updated: new contrast ramp tokens defined and mapped to existing component tokens
Component specs updated: focus-zone rules for composite controls with explicit keyboard flows and roving tabindex alternatives
ARIA-live documentation: pattern examples for virtualized lists (row add/remove/update), clear guidance for politeness and region placement
Prototype validated with NVDA and VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and two accessibility reviewers have signed off
VPAT evidence bundle created: narrative, test matrix, screenshots, automated axe-core report and manual test notes
Engineering acceptance: at least one GH PR created and linked with automated accessibility CI job that runs axe against Storybook examples
comments: 2026-03-10 - MC: Kickoff audit completed. Baseline run of axe + manual checks across 18 components. Key hits: inconsistent tabindex pattern, missing aria-live on table row status updates, contrast failures for muted text on compact charts.

2026-03-11 - AR: Drafted focus-zone pattern with fallback for roving tabindex. Added two variants: 'group-focus' using role=group and explicit focus management, and 'roving' using aria-activedescendant. Seeking feedback from Eng on implementation complexity.
2026-03-11 - LC (Eng lead): Prefer 'roving' for large lists due to performance but need clear guidance for forms and composite widgets. Will allocate ENG-20418 for runtime helper utilities.
2026-03-12 - PM (Owen Patel): Please ensure VPAT narrative distinguishes behavior across browsers (Safari VoiceOver differences). Add user-testing with iOS VoiceOver to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 - AR: Added sample code snippets and Storybook examples. Opened PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/1372
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Use roving-tabindex by default for virtualized lists due to better performance and simpler DOM diffing. Document group-focus as fallback for complex composite widgets.
2026-03-11: Contrast ramp will adopt a +10% lightness delta for disabled/muted states and introduce 'contrast-critical' token for WCAG-critical text overlays on charts.

2026-03-12: ARIA-live regions for virtualized lists will be appended outside virtualization container to avoid screen reader truncation; politeness default = polite for non-blocking updates, assertive only for error states per pattern.
2026-03-12: VPAT will include both automated axe reports and manual test notes for NVDA/VoiceOver across latest two major browser versions.
2026-03-12: Engineering to ship a Storybook compliance suite that the CI can run against; ENG-20418 created as dependency.
next_steps: Finalize token mappings and create a small PR to replace three low-contrast tokens (disabled-label, hint-text, chart-annotation)
Complete Storybook examples for roving and group-focus patterns and add keyboard test harness
Run focused NVDA + VoiceOver sessions with two participants and capture notes
Produce VPAT evidence bundle and upload to Confluence page
Coordinate with ENG to land ENG-20418 and expose runtime helper for roving-tabindex
test_plan: Automated: axe-core run in CI against new Storybook stories (edge, chrome, firefox)
Manual: NVDA (Windows 10), VoiceOver (macOS + iOS), TalkBack (Android) smoke tests on updated components
Contrast: generate contrast report for all tokens using accessible-colors script and verify 3:1 and 4.5:1 thresholds where applicable
Regression: run keyboard-only navigation scenarios for dense table, action menu, inline editor, and charts with data-point focus
